declaredBounds: The three-surface bind still has NO plane verb: mpdTeamActions exposes `unfence` but nothing that re-points `executorRef`/`owner`, so the TEAM record file is patched directly (atomic temp+rename) and verified by re-reading it through `mpdTeams.get` (or from the file when no plane service exists). Declared architectural debt from the prior PASS; F2 narrows its blast radius (compare-and-set) but does not remove it.

The compare-and-set catches a writer that commits inside the synchronous window; the window contains no await, so no JS concurrency can enter it in this process, and the re-read is the last statement before the rename. A commit that lands AFTER the rename is not covered by this compare (the post-write read-back verifies the seat row only).

Today's TeamRecord carries no top-level `revision`/`updatedAt`, so the member-roster sha256 is the always-present half of the fingerprint; the `revision` and `updatedAt` halves are implemented and the revision half is exercised by the `a8-revision` arm (a seeded record carrying `revision: 1`), while no LIVE record currently carries either field.

A plane read that throws at the bind's SNAPSHOT is classified `team-record-unreadable` (F1); a throw at the post-write READ-BACK still travels through the post-spawn-throw branch (`after the child started`, A5) because the write already landed and nothing can be overwritten any more.

The A7 control (no record file) and the A8 control (no external write) are guards for the fixed code; like every arm they are red on HEAD only because the pre-fix code does not bind at all (`seat-rebound` is absent), not because the control itself encodes a defect.
